brief: Something to keep my sewing supplies tidy.

requirements.requirement: Keep sewing supplies tidy - provide compartmented storage
requirements.evidence: 3 hex bases (piece:0,0,0; piece:0,1,0; piece:1,0,0) with 3 bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments) + 2x hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments each) = 7 compartments total for sorting small sewing notions

Bins staged with small-compartment props (heap-screws-div3, heap-nuts-div3, tweezers, tape-electrical) to demonstrate sorting; no dedicated sewing props (thread spools, scissors, fabric) exist in catalog, so generic small workshop props used as proxies. Top-down view (polar 10) shows compartments clearly; side view hides below rim due to deep bins

finish.summary: Built a compact 3-cell hexagonal organiser with 7 compartments across 3 bins (3+2+2) - ideal for buttons, bobbins, needles, etc. Caps and joint bolts applied for finished structure. Staged with small-parts props to illustrate tidy sorting; viewed from above all compartments are visible.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
